newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Q1 housing starts rise 20 percent.
newsitem.headline: Canada Q1 housing starts rise 20 percent.

text.p: Canadian housing starts rose by 20 percent in the first quarter of 1997 to a seasonally adjusted annual rate (SAAR) of 155,200 units from 129,300 units in the last quarter of 1996, the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corp (CMHC) said on Wednesday.
A Reuter survey of economists had forecast housing starts of 152,000 units.
Actual housing starts fell to 22,774 in the first quarter from 32,446 the month before. The SAAR is a monthly figure adjusted to remove normal seasonal variation and multiplied by 12.

The housing corporation said the new housing market gained momentum in the first quarter of 1997.

"While recent increases in mortgage rates may dampen housing starts slightly over the new few months, employment gains are expected to compensate over the long term," senior economist Michel Laurence said in a statement.
